chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Subah ibn Sayyaba, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

What are you and the disavowal? Some of you disavow others. Indeed, the believers, some of them are superior to some, and some of them are more frequent in prayer than some, and some of them have keener insight than some, and these are the ranks.

key_terms.الدَّرَجَات: Ranks or levels of spiritual standing.
key_terms.الْبَرَاءَة: Disavowal or dissociation, often referring to distinguishing between believers and non-believers or among believers themselves.

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of Bara'ah among believers and how are spiritual ranks determined?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that al-Bara'ah among believers is not mere estrangement but a recognition of hierarchical spiritual ranks (darajat) based on varying degrees of devotion, prayer frequency, and insight. This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the Shia understanding that superiority in faith is meritocratic, rooted in individual piety and spiritual acuity rather than uniformity. It contextualizes the social dynamics of the early Muslim community where distinct levels of spiritual authority and practice were acknowledged as divinely ordained distinctions.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Al Sabbah Bin Sayaba, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘What are you and the disavowing (Tabarra)? Some of you are disavowing (Tabarra) from the others. The Momins, some of them are superior to some, and some of them are more frequent of the Salāt than some, and some of them are of more accomplished insight than some, and these are the levels’.
en.sarwar: 4. It is narrated from him (Muhammad ibn Yahya) from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Muhammad ibn Sinan from al-Sabah ibn Siyabah from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

What is this disavowing and disassociation of yours? There are those of you who renounce the others. Among the believers there are those who are better than others. Among them there are those who pray more, and others are of shaip insight. Such are the degrees of belief.”
